actions.text: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 402 - 8 (Roll no. 287). (text: CR H4682-4684)
Passed/agreed to in House: On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 402 - 8 (Roll no. 287). (text: CR H4682-4684)
Considered as unfinished business. (consideration: CR H4692)

At the conclusion of debate, the Yeas and Nays were demanded and ordered. Pursuant to the provisions of clause 8, rule XX, the Chair announced that further proceedings on the motion would be postponed.
DEBATE - The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 2659.
Considered under suspension of the rules. (consideration: CR H4682-4685)
Mr. Garbarino moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill.

committees.name: Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee

dimensions.assessment: Directly involves federal agencies, security personnel, Sector Risk Management Agencies, and critical infrastructure owners and operators nationwide.
dimensions.evidence: establish a joint interagency task force... to facilitate collaboration and coordination among the Sector Risk Management Agencies

dimensions.assessment: Imposes structural coordination, information sharing, and mandatory reporting and briefing requirements on federal departments regarding critical infrastructure threats.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 540 days after the establishment of the task force, the task force shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees the first report

dimensions.assessment: The source material does not state specific appropriations or funding amounts for the task force.
Creates a new multi-agency task force with specific reporting mandates and interagency coordination powers, while exempting it from FACA and the Paperwork Reduction Act.
dimensions.evidence: establish a joint interagency task force (in this section referred to as the 'task force') to facilitate collaboration

dimensions.assessment: Requires an initial report, annual reports for five years, and a termination date tied to the final briefing.
dimensions.evidence: The task force, and all the authorities of this section, shall terminate on the date that is 60 days after the final briefing

missing_information: Specific funding amounts or budgetary allocations required to operate the task force.
importance_detail.rationale: Establishes a joint interagency task force led by CISA to coordinate security efforts against Chinese state-sponsored cyber actors across federal departments and critical infrastructure sectors, requiring regular reporting to Congress over a multi-year period.
